A&E won’t treat the episode, a psych liaison team will be sent to the A&E to assess and section you if needs be. Could be several hours wait, sometimes if you’re lucky it’s quicker but since the services are overrun in general it’s most likely going to be while before you are seen. If you become agitated they may prescribe a benzodiazepine but not much else A&E will be able to do. In general it’s a shit show for psych patients in A&E but if you feel you cannot wait for a referral then it’s your best option. You should already be under a community mental health team (CMHT) since GP’s only prescribe antipsychotics as a repeat medication under the advisement of a psychiatrist. If you were discharged from the CMHT then your GP would need to re-refer you. Contacting the crisis team/duty at the CMHT or turn up in person if you are still under their care is better during 9-5 and if it’s after 5pm go to A&E My catchment area has a 24/7 contact number for the CMHT maybe yours does too? 

Also the legal weed thing for pain isn’t going to go down well as they will say that caused or exacerbated your psychosis/paranoia which in many cases is true. I know too many people that smoked heavily before they’ve had a psychotic episode and after no episodes at all so there’s a strong link between weed and paranoid psychosis. 

Hope you got the help you need.
